warning: These dated notes are lookup aids, not a live policy check. Each entry records the date its official page was read. Reopen the official source for the exact venue/year/track, and the specific journal's instructions where a publisher-wide page is listed. If unavailable, report current policy NOT CHECKED.

sources.scope: Elsevier researcher guidance for highlights; journal exceptions apply
sources.summary: General guidance: 3–5 bullets (Cell Press 3–4), at most 85 characters including spaces per bullet. Consult the specific journal guide.

sources.scope: Elsevier journal manuscript preparation guidance; check journal-specific requirements
sources.summary: Distinguishes basic spelling/grammar/punctuation checks from broader AI-assisted preparation. Check disclosure scope and placement before references; describe actual use and completed human review.

sources.scope: ICMJE Recommendations, Section V.A (Use of AI by Authors); relevant where a medical journal follows the ICMJE Recommendations, subject to that journal's own instructions
sources.summary: Journals should require authors to disclose at submission whether AI-assisted technologies were used, describing the use in both the cover letter and the appropriate section of the submitted work. AI tools should not be listed as authors. Humans remain responsible for the submitted material, should review and edit AI output, ensure attribution with full citations, and should not reference AI-generated material as a primary source.

sources.scope: Springer Nature policy page on AI use in manuscript preparation; journal- and imprint-specific pages may add requirements
sources.summary: Groups AI uses into permitted, conditional and not-permitted tiers. Listing AI as an author is not permitted. Authors describe their AI use and confirm accountability; AI-assisted visual content needs an AI Declaration and disclosure in the caption or legend. Authors remain fully accountable for the submission and must ensure references are real and have been checked.

sources.scope: Taylor & Francis AI Policy for journal and book authors, editors and reviewers; individual journals may restrict AI use further
sources.summary: Generative AI tools must not be listed as authors. Authors must acknowledge any use within the article or book, giving the full tool name with version, how it was used and why; article submissions include a specific AI usage disclosure statement. The policy lists uses that are not permitted and tells authors to check journal instructions, since some journals allow only language improvement.

sources.scope: ICLR 2026 author guide; not a rule for other years or venues
sources.summary: A significant LLM role in ideation or writing that contributes to the work calls for a usage section; the guide allows an appendix outside the page limit. Check the exact author guide for applicability.

sources.scope: NeurIPS 2026 Main Track Handbook, version 2026.3; not other tracks
sources.summary: Describe important, original or non-standard methodological LLM/agent use in the experimental setup or equivalent. Routine grammar/editing/basic coding assistance is distinguished. Authors remain responsible; review-manipulation instructions are prohibited.
